name: Public speaking course

lead: Public speaking courses and clubs teach you to deliver speeches and take feedback, building confidence and delivery for a more commanding presence.

Repeated practice in front of audiences, with peer or instructor feedback, is the route. Clubs such as Toastmasters International use peer evaluation and impromptu speaking. Studies cited on Wikipedia associate teaching public speaking with greater self-confidence, though direct research on anxiety reduction is limited.

paras: People join a club, school class or commercial course and give speeches regularly over weeks or months.
No harms are documented beyond cost and time.

chain: Repeated practice in front of audiences
angle.text: Repeated practice in front of audiences lowers anxiety and sharpens delivery, so you come across with more confident presence. Confidence gains are reported for such training.

lead: A public speaking course is structured training in delivering speeches to a live audience, offered by clubs, schools and commercial providers. It appears in self-improvement and presence-focused culture as a way to build confidence and delivery.

Public speaking has a long history in rhetoric, from Aristotle and Cicero onward, and fear of it (glossophobia) is often cited as a common phobia.[1] Clubs such as Toastmasters International use peer evaluation and impromptu speaking practice.[1] Studies cited on Wikipedia associate teaching public speaking with greater self-confidence, though direct research on anxiety reduction is limited.[1]
